items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: And when I was five years old, Gene Krupa gave me a drum lesson on my dad’s T.V. show.

ctx.x: Most definitely. Steve Condos, who is part of the famous Condos Brothers dance team. When I was four years old, my dad taught me pulse and groove from a bass player, and

then I learned rhythms and accents from a tap dancer. So that’s a unique way to approach the drums. And the gentleman that took Davy Tough’s place in the Woody Herman band with my father, his name is Don Lamond, he’s still with us, very healthy and happy in Orlando, Florida, and still playing great, and he definitely taught me a lot about just the technique of the drumset. I also worked out with Roy Burns for a while when I was around the ages of six and seven or so. And when I was five years old, Gene Krupa gave…

Yeah, I can agree with that. And it’s good because that whole tradition of the swing era, you know, eventually those fellows will all be gone. We hate to think about it. But guys like yourself can keep that thing going.
